question: The Global Partnership for Education (GPE) is the leading multilateral fund for strengthening education systems in low-income countries. Its Replenishment Conference will take place in New York on 23 September 2026, at a time when international funding for education is contracting following cuts by several major donors.

Against this backdrop, the number of children out of school has risen for the seventh consecutive year, reaching 273 million. This trend risks undermining the right to education and jeopardising the achievement of UN Sustainable Development Goal 4. However, education remains a strategic investment for inclusive growth, gender equality, resilience, peace and stability.

A further reduction in financial support would risk reversing decades of progress, particularly in conflict-affected countries. The EU is a long-standing partner of the GPE and its second-largest donor, having allocated EUR 700 million for the period 2021-2027. However, its orientations for the next funding cycle remain unclear. In the light of the above: 1.
What position will the Commission take ahead of the GPE Replenishment Conference?
Will it commit to maintaining at least the current level of support for the GPE?
How will it ensure that education remains a priority of EU external action and the future multiannual financial framework?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (31.8.2026) The EU has long been a steadfast and reliable partner of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE), and this close cooperation remains essential in reinforcing and complementing EU support to partner countries.

President of the European Commission pledged EUR 700 million to GPE for the period 2021–20271, and the Commission remains fully committed to honouring that pledge. This represents an average contribution of EUR 100 million per year and already covers 2026 and 2027, the first two years of GPE’s next financing cycle.

Education remains a longstanding priority of the EU’s external action and a key pillar of the Global Gateway strategy2. Continued support for education and skills development in partner countries — including vocational education and training, within a lifelong learning approach — will therefore remain of central importance.

With regard to the next funding cycle, however, the Commission cannot prejudge the outcome of the negotiations and programming decisions under the Multiannual Financial Framework 2028-2034 and is therefore not in a position, at this stage, to make commitments beyond 2027.
